voluntad_anticipada: No (not among the 15 states with one, as of July 2024)
reasons: Jalisco is the country's leading milk producer, with just over 20% of national output, much of it in Los Altos. Large dairy operations are one of the farm settings where barbiturate euthanasia is used, because the animal is valuable and leaves the food chain anyway.|Jalisco is the main centre of charrería (about 130 of the 900 associations in the national federation; UNESCO heritage since 2016). Horses, stud farms and elite cattle are where pentobarbital is standard: licensed death for animals of high value.|One of the country's largest metropolitan areas, with a dense companion-animal clinical market.|A contrasting legal and moral setting to CDMX: no Ley de Voluntad Anticipada, a 2009 constitutional reform protecting life from conception, and organised Catholic opposition.|University of Guadalajara (with its veterinary school) and ITESO as possible institutional anchors.
considerations: Pentobarbital is not routine in pig production: it is costly, controlled, and leaves the carcass unusable for rendering or meat. Farm use concentrates where the animal is valuable and already outside the food chain. What happens to carcasses after barbiturate euthanasia is itself a research question. Check whether Jalisco has passed a Ley de Voluntad Anticipada since 2024.
sources: SADER Jalisco via BM Editores (April 2023); México Desconocido (December 2016); Catholic News Agency (March 2009); TV Azteca (July 2024)

role: Border interface: where transnational circulation becomes observable
voluntad_anticipada: No (not among the 15 states with one, as of July 2024)
reasons: The post centres Mexico's role in the transnational circulation of pentobarbital and cross-border assisted dying. Tijuana is where that circulation can be observed on the ground.|On the border with San Diego, at some of the busiest crossings in the hemisphere, so both customs regimes (ANAM and US CBP) are present and the drug's change of status between two legal systems happens in one place.|Already in the documentary record: journalism on veterinary pentobarbital and US enforcement names border cities such as Tijuana, giving a documented starting point.|A long-standing US-facing pharmacy economy shows, in everyday practice, the gap between Mexican and US classifications.|Completes the comparison with the two main sites: where the drug is classified (CDMX), where its veterinary uses meet the value of the animal (Guadalajara), and where it crosses a border.
considerations: Study the border, not 'suicide tourism': scope the work as regulation, enforcement, commerce and narratives, never acquisition. Needs a safety and ethics protocol; can combine short field visits with documentary and digital work.
sources: US Attorney's Office, N.D. Illinois (2024; 2025); AVMA; TV Azteca (July 2024)
